The main focus over the next few days will be the remnants of Invest
(94W/95W...as 95W was re-designated today by JTWC after 94W was
cancelled yesterday). This feature will be decaying as it heads up
this way, but sufficient lift via elevated remnant vorticity centers
and deep moisture advection will increase rainfall potential from
south to north starting Saturday, persisting through the remainder of
the weekend. Modest omegas are seen in the time height series
suggesting a few claps of thunder can't be ruled out either,as PWATs
(Precipitable Water Values) climb from current values near 1.5 inches
to 2.3 inches over the weekend. Then, as we head towards the middle
of next week, drier conditions will return to the region.

Marine...
Seas and surf have subsided sufficiently to allow the High Surf and
Small Craft Advisories to be cancelled. However, a High Risk of Rip
Currents remains in effect for our east facing reefs, where surf will
top out near 9 feet. The models showed a 2 foot drop in seas and
easterly swell Sunday night/Monday morning, but feel this may be a
little too quick of a reduction rate, so we went a foot above
guidance for that period to allow for a "smoother" transition in surf
and overall sea height.

Tropical Systems...
The 4 pm position was 8.7N 138.9E. This is 80 miles southeast of 
Yap, 100 miles east-southeast of Ngulu, and 110 miles southwest of 
Ulithi. Hagupit is moving west-northwest at 15 mph. Latest forecast 
track for Hagupit takes the storm west-northwest, passing between Yap
Proper and Ngulu late tonight. Hagupit looks to strengthen a little 
more, with maximum winds of 50 mph (45 kt). Hagupit looks to remain a
tropical storm through at least Monday. those in the path of Hagupit
should continue to monitor forecasts for any possible changes in 
movement or intensity.

For more information on Tropical Storm Hagupit, please refer to 
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) under WMO 
header WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO 
header WTPQ31 PGUM and WTPQ81 PGUM.

A weak tropical disturbance is seen over eastern Micronesia, JTWC's 
Invest 95W, centered just north of Pohnpei near 8N158E. Invest 95W is
moving slowly west-northwest, and is currently sub-low, meaning
development into a significant tropical cyclone is not expected over
the next few days. Latest model guidance is not too keen on 
developing 95W, showing the disturbance dissipating within the next 
around the middle of next week after moving through Chuuk State. 
Even though 95W is not expected to strengthen, residents of islands
between Pohnpei and Weno, Chuuk should monitor forecasts for any
indication of possible development.

Eastern Micronesia...
The pattern remains very active across eastern Micronesia this
afternoon. A weak tropical disturbance, Invest 95W, is found near
8N158E, just north of Pohnpei. 95W is generating numerous showers and
isolated thunderstorms across Pohnpei, with scattered showers over
Kosrae expected to increase to numerous locally heavy showers
Saturday morning. As 95W moves toward the west-northwest, convection
will decrease first over Kosrae, with scattered showers by Saturday
night and isolated early next week. For Pohnpei, however, convection
will be a bit slower to decrease, with numerous locally heavy 
showers continuing through Sunday, then slowly decreasing into next
week.

For Majuro, a broad, weak Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) over
the Marshall Islands will produce a brief period of numerous showers
and isolated thunderstorms Saturday as a weak trade-wind trough
interacts with the ITCZ. As the trough moves off to the west,
convection will decrease, though an overall wet pattern looks to
continue through the middle of next week as the ITCZ remains over 
the Marshalls.

For the marine environment, seas will remain below hazardous levels
of 10 feet, though choppy seas are likely for Pohnpei and Kosrae due
to gusty winds with convection and gentle to moderate trade winds.
Gentle to moderate winds look to continue through the weekend for
Majuro and through Saturday afternoon for Pohnpei and Kosrae.

Western Micronesia...
Tropical Storm Hagupit continues to move west-northwestward across 
Yap State and has moved northwest of Sorol, making its approach
towards Yap Proper. The 4 pm position was 8.7N 138.9E, about 80 
miles to the southeast. Tropical Storm Hagupit (05W) currently has 
maximum sustained winds of 45 mph and is forecast to move through or 
just south of Yap Proper tonight, slightly intensifying to 50 mph 
maximum sustained winds. Tropical storm force winds are expected 
across Yap Proper and adjacent coastal waters through Saturday 
morning. Building northeast to east swell is expected to produce 
dangerous surf of up to 16 ft along north and east facing reefs 
through Saturday morning, then is expected to fall below the 15 foot 
threshold, but is still expected to remain hazardous through at least
late Saturday afternoon. Mino
